=================== underwrite README # Underwrite **A team of AI agents that does venture due diligence while you sleep, and checks its own work.** Give it a list of startups. An **analyst agent** decides what to look up, reads sources and records every fact with the exact sentence it came from; facts that don't match their source are bounced back to it on the spot. A **skeptic agent** attacks the result and sends the analyst back until the evidence holds up. A **watcher** re-checks every company each night and re-investigates only what changed. A **coach agent** reads all of this from [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) traces, rewrites the agents' prompts, and keeps a change only if the eval score goes up. **Live site (memo gallery + scoreboard):** https://hacker-git-code.github.io/underwrite-/  ·  Built for **#neatHack** (Oct 10–12, 2026), theme: *"Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching."*

Each memo is a three-page dossier modelled on Sequoia's famous 1977 evaluation form for Apple: **page 1** an evaluation form (typed labels, hand-written answers, red circled source numbers, a VERIFIED stamp, conflicts noted in the margin), **page 2** a typed memorandum with the full analysis, **page 3** an appendix with every source, the claims it supports, the claims that were rejected, and the agent's run log. Download as PDF, or page 1 as PNG. --- ## Contents - [What it does](#what-it-does) - [Why you can trust it unattended](#why-you-can-trust-it-unattended) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Self-improvement: the Coach and neatlogs](#self-improvement-the-coach-and-neatlogs) - [Results](#results) - [Sponsor tools and how each is used](#sponsor-tools-and-how-each-is-used) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [Commands](#commands) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Running it unattended on AWS](#running-it-unattended-on-aws) - [Project layout](#project-layout) - [Evidence checklist for judges](#evidence-checklist-for-judges) - [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) - [Limitations and roadmap](#limitations-and-roadmap) ## What it does A real run (Ramp, agent mode), shortened: ``` $ underwrite run "Ramp" --domain ramp.com [recover ] gemini-3.8-flash failed (daily quota exhausted); falling back to gemini-3.5-flash [recover ] gemini-3.5-flash failed (daily quota exhausted); falling back to groq:openai/gpt-oss-120b [plan ] 10 questions, 20 queries for Ramp [agent ] step 1 -> company_profile() [agent ] step 2 -> record_claim(field='founded_year', value='2019', evidence_id='E1') → ACCEPTED C1 [agent ] step 4 -> web_search('Ramp founders CEO Eric Glyman Karim Atiyeh') [agent ] step 5 -> record_claim(field='ceo', 'Eric Glyman and Karim Atiyeh serve as Co-CEOs', evidence_id='E7') ... [agent ] round 1 ended on budget after 24 steps [verify ] judge: 11 supported, 0 partial, 0 rejected of 11 [skeptic ] objection: key traction numbers rely on a single low-authority source [skeptic ] objection: no evidence on risks or controversies - a priority-1 question [skeptic ] sending the analyst back for round 2 [agent ] step 25 -> web_search('Ramp customer count revenue 70,000 Bloomberg TechCrunch') [agent ] step 27 -> web_search('Ramp lawsuits controversy security incident regulatory issues') [extract ] C13 In May 2025, a Congressman investigated Ramp over its attempt to win a $25 million federal contract [verify ] claim rejected in-loop: quote not in E20 (match 53%) — agent must fix it [verify ] self-corrected: C14 accepted after the agent fixed a rejected claim [agent ] step 40 -> finish(...) [memo ] done in 212s · 15 claims · 93% supported · 11 Crustdata credits · 2 recoveries ``` Nobody told it to look for a congressional investigation: the skeptic objected that risks were unexamined, and the analyst went and found one. It also found that Ramp's CEO had just made his co-founder co-CEO, with the source linked. A first-pass diligence memo takes an analyst hours. Underwrite produces one in 3–5 minutes for about 11–19 Crustdata credits, and the LLM side runs on free tiers. ### Three agents, one loop | Agent | Decides | Guardrails around it | |---|---|---| | **Analyst** (tool-calling loop) | which tool to call next: `company_profile`, `web_search`, `read_page`, `record_claim`, `update_question`, `add_question`, `finish` | every claim is grounded against its cited source **the moment it is recorded** and bounced back if the quote isn't there; budgets shown after every action; `finish` refused while priority-1 questions are open; old page text compacted out of context; c | **Skeptic** | whether the evidence is good enough, or which 1–4 objections must be fixed first | sees only what an investment committee would see; can send the analyst back while rounds and budget remain | | **Watcher** (nightly) | whether a company changed since its memo (fresh Crustdata record diff + news since the memo) | re-investigation is scoped to one new priority-1 question, seeded with the previous verified claims | | **Coach** (offline) | how to rewrite the agents' prompts, based on neatlogs traces, detections and eval failures | a change is kept only if the eval improves on the train split at sane cost; test split held out | The original fixed pipeline (plan → search → extract → verify → write) is kept as `--mode pipeline`, as the baseline the agents are measured against. ## Why you can trust it unattended | Risk when nobody is watching | What Underwrite does | |---|---| | The model invents a fact | Every claim must carry a quote from one evidence block. Code checks that the quote is really in that source (fuzzy match ≥ 90%); claims that fail are rejected **without** asking a model. | | The quote exists but doesn't prove the claim | A separate judge prompt sees only the claim, the quote, and the source text around it, and rules supported / partial / unsupported. Only supported and partial claims reach the memo. | | Sources disagree | Verified values are clustered per fact (founding year, headcount, funding, HQ, CEO); more than one cluster is a **conflict**, written in red in the memo's margin (e.g. *"Crustdata says 18 employees, the website says 50"*). | | The memo cites something unverified | Citations to claims that didn't pass verification are stripped before rendering, and counted. | | An API fails (429, 5xx, timeout, empty page) | Exponential backoff with jitter, honouring `Retry-After`; Crustdata search → DuckDuckGo fallback; Crustdata fetch → direct fetch fallback. | | A model is down, overloaded, or out of quota | Each role has a chain of models across providers (Gemini → Gemini → Groq → Cerebras → Claude on Bedrock). Dead models are skipped for the rest of the run; overloaded ones cool down for 2 minutes. | | The model returns broken JSON | A cheap repair call fixes it against the JSON Schema instead of failing the run. | | The machine crashes mid-run | State is checkpointed after every phase and after **every analyst tool step**; `underwrite resume ` continues mid-investigation. cited memo + fact sheet] =================== aarush323 README # Loadline (NeatHacks) **Loadline** boots a repo’s app in Docker, load-tests the HTTP APIs, and runs an **Investigator** agent that reads the code and writes an evidence-backed report (or a clear **blocked** reason). **Onboarding:** [setup.md](setup.md) — install, `.env`, blind eval, FastAPI blocker, absolute paths. ### Commands (from Loadline repo root) ```bash uv run loadline load --repo /absolute/path/to/app # trial boot → save config (stderr progress; --quiet) uv run loadline run --repo /absolute/path/to/app # boot → investigator → report.md (--fast, --verbose) uv run loadline dashboard # TTY run browser uv run loadline dashboard --serve # web UI on :8123 uv run loadline doctor --check-model && uv run loadline doctor --cleanup ``` | Command | One line | |---------|----------| | **`loadline load`** | “Can we boot this repo? Save the boot config.” | | **`loadline run`** | “Boot it, investigate under load, write the report.” | | **`loadline dashboard`** | “Browse past runs (terminal or `--serve`).” | `run` does **not** call `load`. You run `load` yourself when you want a saved config before a full run. **Primary integration target (blind):** `integration/targets/unreliable-blind` — see [setup.md](setup.md) §5. --- ## Step 0 — your `.env` (Loadline on your laptop) Before either command, set up **this repo’s** `.env` (copy from `.env.example`). That is **not** the app under test; it is **keys and settings for Loadline**: - **LLM:** `LOADLINE_MODEL` plus `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (required for `loadline run`, not for `load` today). - **Optional:** `NEATLOGS_*` for traces. Check: `uv run loadline doctor` (add `--check-model` before a real `run`). The **target app’s** env (Compose, `.env` for Postgres, test users, etc.) is what `load` / `run` figure out when they **boot**—see below. --- ## Workflow: `loadline load` **Goal:** Prove the repo can boot and **write a small config file** so the next `run` does not have to guess as much. **No LLM investigator. No `report.md`.** ```bash uv run loadline load /path/to/app-repo # optional: also copy config into the repo uv run loadline load /path/to/app-repo --write-to-repo ``` ### What happens (steps) 1. **Docker check** — Is the daemon up? If not → `blocked`, stop. 2. **Discover** — Is there a `docker-compose` file or Dockerfile? If neither → `blocked`, stop. 3. **Resolve** — Pick compose file, app service, container port, health path (from repo layout + optional `.loadline.yaml` hints). If Loadline cannot pick a single HTTP app → `blocked`, stop. 4. **Trial boot** — Start the stack, wait until health checks pass, then **tear it down** (`teardown=True`). This boot is thrown away; it is only a proof. 5. **Write config** — Save `loadline.yaml` under Loadline’s home dir (`LOADLINE_HOME/configs/...`). With `--write-to-repo`, also write `.loadline.yaml` in the app repo. Output is a path like `wrote .../loadline.yaml`, not a performance report. **Progress:** `load` prints steps on **stderr** by default (Docker → discover → resolve → trial boot with compose/health ticks → write config). Use **`--quiet`** to hide progress; blockers still print. ### Setup agent (planned, not the default path today) Today, `load` is **deterministic** (steps above only). We plan a **setup agent** for repos where boot is ambiguous—for example login/auth not described, or unclear “prepare” commands (migrations, seed scripts). That agent would loop with its own small tools (`check_config`, `try_boot`, `write_config`), still **without** running the Investigator or k6 experiments. `loadline run` will **never** call that agent; only `load` will. Until that lands, use `load` for the trial boot + saved yaml, or hand-edit `.loadline.yaml` when you already know the service/port/health path. --- ## Workflow: `loadline run` **Goal:** Boot the app **for real**, run the **Investigator** agent, save **`report.md`**, then clean up Docker. ```bash uv run loadline run /path/to/app-repo ``` ### What happens (steps) 1. **Preflight** — Confirm model API keys are set. Missing key → exit before Docker. 2. **Boot** — `boot_and_prepare`: start Compose (using hints, repo `.loadline.yaml`, and/or saved config from `load`). Wait until the app is healthy. Stack **stays running** for the next phase. Failure → **blocker** printed, artifacts under `run_dir`, teardown as needed. 3. **Investigate** — Investigator **agent loop** (see next section). Uses the booted network and only allowed internal hosts. 4. **Report** — The agent’s **last message** is written to `report.md` (and minimal `report.json`). Printed to the terminal unless you pass `--no-report-print`. 5. **Teardown** — Stop containers/networks/volumes labelled for this run. ### `loadline dashboard` After you have runs under `$LOADLINE_HOME/runs/`: ```bash uv run loadline dashboard uv run loadline dashboard --run uv run loadline dashboard --serve --port 8123 ``` --- ## Investigator agent loop (`loadline run` only) After boot, one **Pydantic AI** agent runs with **three tools**. This is the “main loop” for capacity investigation. **Starting prompt (idea):** *The app is booted. Find which endpoints break under load and why, using code and `run_k6`. ﻿# JobReady

An AI-powered adaptive interview preparation agent built for neatHack 2026.

## What it does

JobReady helps job seekers prepare for interviews using their CV, target job description, and personalised practice sessions.

## Core features

- Analyse a candidate's CV and job description
- Generate relevant interview questions
- Evaluate candidate responses
- Ask adaptive follow-up questions
- Track interview progress
- Produce a personalised readiness report

## Technology

- PHP 8.2
- HTML, CSS and JavaScript
- Gemini API (default), with optional OpenAI provider
- neatlogs for agent observability

## Project status

Hackathon development in progress.

## Local setup

Requirements: PHP 8.2 with `PDO`, `pdo_sqlite`, `curl`, `fileinfo`, `dom`, `zip`, `zlib`, and `iconv` enabled. Confirm the modules with `php -m`. Document extraction also requires an available PHP CLI executable and `proc_open`.

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and adjust local settings as needed. The example contains placeholders only; credentials belong in `.env` and must not be committed.
2. Install the locked, lightweight document-parser dependency:

   ```sh
   composer install --no-interaction --no-plugins --no-scripts --prefer-dist
   ```

3. Start PHP's built-in server from the repository root, with upload limits sufficient for a 5 MB document and its multipart wrapper:

   ```sh
   php -d upload_max_filesize=5M -d post_max_size=6M -d display_errors=0 -S 127.0.0.1:8000 -t public
   ```

| README can't verify its own claims (grounding rule) | 3 claims "verified" citing only README.md | 0 circular verifications | — |
| Localhost URLs = unknown, not dead; roast must match results (langchain-ai/open_deep_research) | 5/33 dead links (2 were 127.0.0.1 dev URLs); roast called a live video link "dead" | 3/33 dead; roast accurate | audit ids `53fe70e82c21` (before) → `f2b5f750984e` (after) |

## M2 full audits (python -m app.cli <repo> --full)
| Repo | Score | Claims verified | Tokens | Time | Audit id |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| openai/swarm | 27 | 4/7 | 19,066 | 52s | 4c5f0f5b9cf9 |
| huggingface/smolagents | 17 | 1/8 | 15,061 | 37s | 19605ae23560 |
| langchain-ai/open_deep_research | 32 | 4/8 | 21,172 | 34s | f2b5f750984e |

Failure-recovery evidence: every run above hit Groq 429s (8k TPM free tier) and recovered via
backoff → fallback model → wait-for-quota; each retry/fallback is a step + neatlogs event.

## M2.5: two-speed audits, tarball + search_repo, model rotation (2026-10-10)
Before = M2 single-phase audit. After = quick phase + deep phase, two consecutive runs each
(audit ids are neatlogs session ids; the quick and deep traces share them).

| Repo | Before: tokens / time / verified | After run A: quick → deep, verified | After run B: quick → deep, verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| openai/swarm | 19,066 / 52s / 4 of 7 | 4,094 tok, 5.5s → 16,181 tok, 7.6s · **6 of 8** (`3c94ce84b8a5`) | 4,048 tok, 6.1s → 10,145 tok, 30.6s · 3 of 7 (`4d5dbd1bf972`) |
| huggingface/smolagents | 15,061 / 37s / 1 of 8 | 5,812 tok, 47.5s* → 17,896 tok, 49.8s · **6 of 8** (`b8e64c021d56`) | 3,981 tok, 10.4s → 9,960 tok, 30.3s · 3 of 8 (`fa16370b7b8b`) |
| langchain-ai/open_deep_research | 21,172 / 34s / 4 of 8 | 4,024 tok, 11.9s → 18,159 tok, 57.8s · 3 of 8 (`909e4b969177`) | 4,235 tok, 11.7s → 18,682 tok, 80.8s · 4 of 8 (`6dbfbb5d1c76`) |

\* waited for per-minute quota on every model.

- **Time to first result:** 34–52s → **5.5–12s** (quick phase).
- **Verified claims:** smolagents 1/8 → 3–6/8, swarm 4/7 → 3–6/8, open_deep_research 4/8 → 3–4/8.
  It varies run to run with the model the scheduler gets: under quota pressure the weakest
  model (gpt-oss-20b) does more of the judging.
- **What made the difference** (intermediate runs, same day): with the tarball + `search_repo`
  but no pre-search, smolagents verified **0/8** at 20.8k–23.8k deep tokens, because gpt-oss

# Evaluation results

All runs: `claude-haiku` through the neatHack LiteLLM proxy, diagnosis mode (the harness rejects every proposed change, so
only the decision is graded), 12 real faults from `lab/faults/`, one run per scenario per version, 2026-10-10.
Regenerate this table: `python evals/compare.py evals/results/*-diagnose.json` (the newest file per version wins).

## What changed between versions

| Version | Change |
|---|---|
| v1 | Baseline prompt: "investigate, find root cause, propose a fix". Same tools, same policy gate. |
| v2 | + Investigation method from *Systems Performance* 2e (`knowledge/methodology.md`): problem statement, hypotheses, USE method, request path, symptom vs cause. |
| v3 | + Deterministic guard: each proposal declares its expected effect; "no effect" is rejected. Strict rule: propose only real fixes. |
| v4 | Guard relaxed: a safe temporary mitigation is allowed (and the permanent fix is escalated). Process check shows process AGE and parent PID. |
| v5 | + Human-owned fix-compatibility table in `policy.yaml`: restart/start/rollout-restart cannot fix config-class causes (`INCOMPATIBLE_FIX`). It fired 2 times in v5. |

=== underwrite hackathon.md
over the neatlogs MCP server, rewrites the agent's prompts, re-runs the eval set,
- Required tools: neatlogs (tracing + Coach loop), Entire (checkpointed build sessions), cfo.ai (business plan)
  state machine with `resume`; chaos mode; eval harness (12 companies, train/test split); Coach over neatlogs MCP.
  breadth-first queries + 2 searches reserved for the gap round (commit `ab59efd`). Re-run: 9/9 topics, 12 claims, 92% supported.
- Memo redesigned as a paper dossier modelled on Sequoia's 1977 Apple evaluation form (commit `e06539d`).
- v1 baseline eval running (12 companies).
- Script: `submission/DEMO_SCRIPT.md` (video pending)
- [ ] Before/after run comparison with numbers — after the Coach run (`prompts/v2/COACH_NOTES.md`)
- [ ] cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) — inputs ready in `business/PLAN.md`
- Ground truth covers stable facts only; judgement quality isn't auto-scored.
=== underwrite PLAN
# Underwrite: business plan (inputs for cfo.ai)
This is the plan we model in cfo.ai. Numbers marked **measured** come from real runs (`runs/*/state.json`,
`runs/eval-*/eval.json`). Numbers marked **assumption** are ours to defend and are the levers to play with in cfo.ai.
**Why they pay:** a first-pass memo costs an analyst 2–4 hours (at $60–120/hour fully loaded that is $120–480 per
company). Underwrite produces one in about 4 minutes, with every fact sourced and checked, for well under $1 of cost.
| Price per Crustdata credit | $0.02 | **assumption**: Crustdata doesn't publish a self-serve rate; replace with the rate on your plan |
| Data cost per memo | ~$0.36 | 18 × $0.02 |
| LLM cost per memo (paid list price) | ~$0.013 | **measured** at Gemini paid-tier list prices; $0 on free tiers |
| Compute per memo | ~$0.002 | t3.small at $0.0208/h, ~4 min per memo |
| **Total cost per memo** | **~$0.38** | |
| Angel | $49 / month | 25 memos, PDF export | 25 × $0.38 = $9.50 | ~81% |
| Fund | $399 / month | 300 memos, nightly watchlist, 5 seats, Slack digest | 300 × $0.38 = $114 | ~71% |

Report on the 26 repos in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kinnu-neathack/ab623eaf-f207-4102-9002-9ee611c73914/scratchpad/field/` (chunk1). "Trailers" means `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers out of total commits. Nothing was cloned or run; a few evidence files were read through `gh api`.

## Entries with real substance

**haodaz/hioffer**. PhD-application agent: researches program requirements and faculty, drafts tailored materials, verifies its own citations.
- neatlogs: five screenshots in `evidence/neatlogs/` (trace list, tree, detections, the run-1 error); runs tagged `run1`..`run5`. No public trace links.
- Entire: 43/45 trailers, `.entire/`, saved `checkpoint list/explain/tokens` and `entire why` output. No entire-graph.
- cfo.ai: public link (cfo.ai/s/A_qiW6hIGmm-3fDR), four screenshots, results file (Year 1 revenue $98,000, 76.3% margin, pre-seed scenario runs dry August of Year 2).
- Progress: live on Vercel and Railway, one test file. Measured: per-call input tokens 27.4k to 13.6k, about $2.2 to $0.83 per program, seven defects logged across five runs, including a 429 budget exhaustion.
- Gaps: demo is a script and tooling with no video file; posts are drafts.
- Verdict: the most complete evidence set on this list.

**Sher110106/migration-parachute**. Agent runs expand/backfill/contract Postgres migrations, backs off under lock contention, and gates the destructive step on proof and owner approval.
- neatlogs: `neatlogs-before.png` and `neatlogs-after.png` plus JSON replays.
- Entire: 14/25 trailers, checkpoint metadata, two entire-graph JSON outputs.
- cfo.ai: workspace page link plus a verification file with three scenarios (base month-24 MRR $25,410; downside ends at -$98,887 cash).
- Progress: results table is baseline 0 rows kept, v0 4,000, v1 10,000; 12 scenarios with v0 passing 11 and v1 12; LLM planner $0.0094 total. Demo mp4 in a GitHub release.
- Gaps: posts are drafts ("Nothing here has been posted").
- Verdict: strong, with a very clean before/after story.

**sanchit940/nightwatch-agent**. DevOps agent that diagnoses injected incidents and changes infrastructure only through HMAC-bound approvals.
- neatlogs: SDK spans in code; no screenshots or links in the tree.
- Entire: 19/20 trailers, `docs/entire-evidence.md`.
- cfo.ai: inputs file only (pricing $199 and $799, measured cost per incident); no link.
- Progress: 12 real faults across five prompt versions: correct fix decision 67% (v1) to 92% (v5), about $0.059 per incident, 0 unauthorized changes. It reports that root-cause accuracy dropped from 100% to 92%.
- Gaps: posts are drafts, no video, two test files.
- Verdict: strong agent and eval; thin on cfo.ai and neatlogs proof.

**DurgaPritam/neatHack-QBITS- (PreJudge)**. Audits a public repo against the neatHack rubric, checks README claims against code, and returns a score and fix list.
- neatlogs: three public trace links in `EVIDENCE.md` (labels still placeholders).
- Entire: nothing (0 trailers, no `.entire/`).
- cfo.ai: public link (cfo.ai/s/xBCsLLiMtconXUBf) plus `docs/business-plan.md` ($199/$499/$999 tiers, $0.0095 per audit, 97% margin).
- Progress: 39 commits, 18 test files. Measured: 40,086 tokens/106s/0 of 8 verified to 19,066/52s/5 of 7; time to first result 34-52s to 5.5-12s; Groq 429 recovery.
- Verdict: good numbers, but missing a required tool so far. It could be pointed at our repo.

**hacker-git-code/underwrite-**. Analyst, skeptic, watcher and coach agents write sourced venture diligence memos; the coach rewrites prompts from neatlogs traces.
- neatlogs: SDK and MCP use in code; trace ids said to be in dossiers; no screenshots.
- Entire: 12/13 trailers, `graph-agent.md`, `submission/ENTIRE.md`.
- cfo.ai: `business/PLAN.md` is inputs only; the README's own checklist leaves cfo.ai unticked.
- Progress: live GitHub Pages site with memos, 12-company eval run in the tree. The README results table is an "Evaluation in progress" placeholder; before/after and posts are unticked; video pending.
- Verdict: the most ambitious agent, with required evidence still open.

**sourabhnirvani/teamloop**. A crew of bots that controls a Windows laptop from desktop, phone or Telegram, with approval cards.

- Entire: 19/50 trailers, checkpoint lists for both teammates.

**aarush323/NeatHacks (Loadline)**. Boots a repo in Docker, load-tests it with k6, and an investigator agent writes an evidence-backed report.
- neatlogs: setup and probe code, described as optional; no trace was sent.
- Entire: 5/6 trailers; entire-graph is a runtime tool (`loadline/entire_runtime/`).

- Entire: 3/5 trailers; eight entire-graph JSON outputs in `docs/evidence/entire-graph-issue-3/`.

- Progress: 14 test files, no results; patch proposal only just landed.

**JMadhan1/tenantguard**. Reproduces a planted tenant-isolation leak, fixes it, catches its own regressing fix, and proves the final fix.
- neatlogs: code path only. Entire: 0 trailers, no `.entire/`. cfo.ai: `BUSINESS_PLAN.md` written "for cfo.ai", not loaded.
- `docs/EVIDENCE.md` is a template of LINK placeholders. The shown run uses a scripted offline brain. The README's "tests passing" badge is static.
- Verdict: nice recovery story, no sponsor evidence.

**Vex-15/Agent-RedOps**. Runs 11 attack scenarios on a simulated procurement pipeline and re-runs them with guards applied.
- neatlogs: spans in code. Entire: `.entire/` present, 0 trailers. cfo.ai: `BUSINESS_PLAN.md` ($999/mo tier), no cfo.ai artefact.
- Claims 48 pytest tests (one test file). The pipeline is deterministic, so the "agent" is thin.

**AdiGoCrazy/atlas-commerce**. Prototype for regional product ranking from synthetic signals.
- 7/33 trailers, 74 tests passing.
- The README states neatlogs live evidence is blocked (no key) and cfo.ai is "degraded" with local simulation, though `docs/evidence/cfo-ai-harbor-bay.xlsx` exists.

**ibochivincent-lang/proof-of-search-ai (Dala)**. LangGraph research agent with cited reports and SHA-256 source ledger.

**PeytonLi/Conduit**. Planned supplier-delay recovery agent.
- 63 commits, 86 test-related files, 0 trailers.
- README: "No live provider or supplier workflow is enabled"; sponsor tools are mentions only.

## Early or thin

- **techbyFEMI/TestGap-Agent**: finds Python test gaps and drafts tests. 1/10 trailers, an entire-graph note, and a cfo.ai brief that it labels "prepared input, not proof". Drafted tests are not executed yet.
- **angqd/NeatHacks (ToolPrune)**: hierarchical tool retrieval. 6/7 trailers. Eval set frozen, baselines not built, "Hypothesis unproven". No agent, no cfo.ai.
- **davre001/Torque (Suture)**: issue-to-PR agent with trace-driven recovery. The README describes `agents/`, `tools/`, `business/` and `demo/`; the tree has none of them, only `frontend/` and `evidence/README.md`. 2/16 trailers.
- **Misterhoye10/neat-patch**: issue-to-PR "self-healing" agent. Four commits in 37 minutes. The trailers are hand-made ids (for example `chk_model_sunset_healed_...`) and `.entire/checkpoints/*.json` is its own format. The tracer is a custom local file writer. "Live metrics" (3/3 tests, 83% margin) are unsupported.
- **khushi-infinity/factora-agents**: factory digital twin. "No agents, no ML yet". 0 trailers, with the Entire limitation documented; the business plan is "not yet modelled".
- **Thesusxo/JobReady**: PHP interview-prep agent. neatlogs HTTP client, 1/5 trailers, no cfo.ai.
- **SamarthKarnam4246/GhostErase**: document deletion prototype. Two commits. Says Entire is not installed and cfo.ai OAuth is unverified.
- **23f2001033/interlock**: lands multiple AI-written branches and finds changes that fail only together. Three commits: spec and skeleton only.
- **nylxar/readme-liar-detector**: verifies README claims by running them sandboxed. Two commits; evidence folders named but absent.
- **NUNRIBHAC/Neathack-Agent (DisruptRadar)**: three commits and a two-line README.
- **Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence, agent-harness, brand-kit**: three components of one project, TicketStub (the main repo is not on my list). 88, 21 and 7 commits, heavy tests, 0 trailers. Each README says it does not establish "connected sponsor tools".

## Five strongest, ranked

1. **hioffer**: only entry with all three tools evidenced by artefacts, plus a live site and measured before/after cost numbers.
2. **migration-parachute**: crisp three-row results table, entire-graph outputs, neatlogs screenshots, cfo.ai scenarios and a recorded demo.
3. **nightwatch-agent**: best eval rigour (12 real faults, five versions, misses reported) and 19/20 checkpoints, but cfo.ai and neatlogs proof are still thin.
4. **PreJudge (QBITS)**: public neatlogs trace links and a public cfo.ai model with real numbers; no Entire at all.
5. **underwrite**: strongest agent design and a live memo site; its own checklist shows before/after, cfo.ai and posts unfinished.

No repo on this list shows posted #neatHack links; hioffer, parachute and nightwatch have drafts only.

## Overlap with Whodunit

Nobody on this list bisects commit history or uses Entire checkpoints to recover why a change was made. The nearest:

- **interlock**: attributes a combined failure to specific AI-written branches, proves it with a test, and tells the responsible coding agent. Closest in spirit, but only a spec so far.
- **Torque, neat-patch, foreman**: issue to patch to verified fix. Torque's recovery agent reads the failed neatlogs trace, but little of it is built.
- **tenantguard**: reproduce, fix, and prove the fix with a deterministic verifier, on one planted bug.
- **underwrite**: its coach improves the agent from neatlogs traces and keeps a change only if the eval improves. Same "prove it with replays" idea, applied to prompts.
